titulo: Adjectives 2: with ein, mein, kein (ein großer Mann): Nominative and accusative

aula.titulo: Adjectives 2: with ein, mein, kein (ein großer Mann)
aula.objetivo: Give the adjective its ending after ein, eine, mein, dein, kein…: the adjective takes -er, -e, -es where the article doesn't show the case, and -en everywhere else.

blocos.titulo: Ein, mein, kein + adjective, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «ein», «eine», «mein», «kein»… fail to show the case in THREE places: masculine nominative («ein»), neuter nominative («ein») and neuter accusative («ein»). In those places the ADJECTIVE takes over and shows the case: «ein großer Mann» (-er, like the -r of «der»), «ein kleines Kind» (-es, like the -s of «das»). STEP 2: everywhere else, the article already shows the case, and the adjective takes «-e» or «-en», just as after «der»: «eine kleine Frau», «einen großen Mann». STEP 3: nominative: ein großer Mann (-er), eine kleine Frau (-e), ein neues Auto (-es), meine neuen Autos (-en). STEP 4: accusative: einen großen Mann (-en), eine kleine Frau (-e), ein neues Auto (-es), meine neuen Autos (-en). STEP 5: rule of thumb: «-er» and «-es» appear only when «ein» has no ending: masculine nominative, and neuter nominative and accusative.
blocos.comparacao: English has nothing like this — "a big man", "a small child". The logic is simple, though: German wants the case to show up ONCE. If the article (ein) didn't show it, the adjective does. Think of it as the -r of «der» and the -s of «das» moving onto the adjective: der → ein großeR, das → ein kleineS.

blocos.enunciado: Describe 6 people or animals with «ein» and an adjective: «Das ist ein netter Mann. Ich habe eine kleine Katze …»
Write the chart of the adjective after der, die, das in all four cases.
